records.title: EVP - Chief Underwriting Officer
records.notes: THE most important contact in this CRM for the escort-discount question. Chief Underwriting Officer of the world's largest P&I club, and named to succeed Mike Hall as chair of the International Group's REINSURANCE COMMITTEE for the 2027/28 renewal — the seat that negotiates the group excess-of-loss programme, $2.25bn above a $100m pool ceiling, with the commercial reinsurance market. This matters because the 2026 war-risk cancellations did not originate with insurers: Gard's own Circular 01/2026 says the club acted because ITS reinsurers served notice on IT. If an escort is ever going to earn a premium discount, the decision sits at the reinsurance layer, and this is the person who sits there. Approach with a loss-reduction argument and evidence, not a sales pitch.

records.source: Gard's own published employee directory page.
records.title: Claims Executive
records.notes: Claims executive rather than underwriting or loss prevention. Useful for understanding how a war-risk claim is actually handled, but not a decision-maker on pricing.

records.title: Vice President, Charterers and Traders and Defence Global
records.notes: Directly relevant, for two reasons. First, under most time and voyage charters the CHARTERER bears the war-risk premium — so charterers are the party with the budget, and our CRM has only one charterer account. She runs that book globally at the largest club. Second, the covers Gard actually cancelled in March 2026 were the non-mutual ones: P&I for Charterers, P&I for Traders, extended crew and deviation liability. That is her portfolio. No email or phone was published on the card supplied; neither has been guessed.

description: One row per named individual at a target account. Collected from each company's own published leadership or management page on 2026-09-05, name and title as published. LinkedIn profile URLs are either published by the company itself or matched from public search results on name plus employer plus title. Nothing was read from behind a login. Pure HR, finance, audit, legal and IT roles are deliberately not collected — they are not a buying role for this product.

record_schema.title: string, as published
record_schema.buying_role: one of: technical-manager, commercial-manager, beneficial-owner, charterer, other
record_schema.seniority: one of: c-suite, director, manager, other
record_schema.linkedin_url: string or null — public profile URL
record_schema.email: string or null — corporate address only
record_schema.email_status: one of: unknown, guessed, verified, bounced
record_schema.status: one of the pipeline values in crm/accounts.json
record_schema.linkedin_source: string or null — how the profile URL was matched

policy: Corporate contact points only. No personal phone numbers, no personal email addresses, no home addresses.
A LinkedIn profile URL is a published professional identifier and may be stored. Nothing scraped from behind a login is stored.
Every person record must carry the source it came from and the date it was retrieved.
Anyone who asks to be removed is deleted, not suppressed.
gaps: 94 people on record against a target of 1,000+.
19 of 38 accounts now have at least one named contact; 19 still have none.

Companies that publish no named leadership at all: Delta Tankers, Navigation Maritime Bulgare (Navibulgar), Allseas Marine, Columbia Shipmanagement, Oldendorff Carriers. For these the only route in is the generic office address or LinkedIn.
16 priority-1 security, DPA, HSQE or fleet roles found. Most companies publish a C-suite and stop there, so the operational buyer is still unnamed at the majority of accounts.
23 of 94 people have a LinkedIn profile attached.
No email address and no email pattern has been derived for any person.
George Petropoulos's employer is listed only as 'Shipping Company' on his profile. Establish which one before approaching.

role_map.note: Which published job titles map to the buying roles in ownership-model.json. Used to rank a POC, not to guess one. CSO added 2026-09-04 after a real profile showed DPA/CSO/HSQE held as one combined role, which appears to be common at Greek managers.

roles.why: The ISPS Code makes the Company Security Officer responsible for the ship security assessment and the ship security plan. This is the role that formally owns whether a vessel takes protective measures. It outranks DPA for our purposes and was missing from the first version of this map.
The ISM Code puts the DPA between ship and top management on safety and security. Named in the Document of Compliance, so this role exists at every manager by law.
Owns the operational decision on a given hull, which is where escort is accepted or refused.
Holds the war risk premium, which is the budget the product competes with.
On time and voyage charters the charterer bears the premium and can specify escort in the fixture.
Route in only at the smaller owners and managers, where the CEO is the operator.

role_map.ranking: Priority 1 is the first approach at a ship manager. Priority 3 is a fallback where the company publishes no operational names.

collection_rules: Published corporate sources only: leadership pages, press releases, annual reports, regulatory filings.
Name and job title as published. Nothing inferred, nothing guessed.
No personal email addresses, personal phone numbers or home addresses. Ever.
A LinkedIn profile URL may be stored as a published professional identifier. Nothing from behind a login is stored.
Every person carries the source URL and the date retrieved.
Delete on request, do not suppress.

conflicts.issue: The 2024 press release was extracted as naming Haakon Lenz as both CEO and COO, and Carl Schou as CEO.
conflicts.resolution: Recorded Lenz as CEO from 1 January 2025 only. Schou continued as senior advisor for six months and is not recorded as a current POC.

warm_first_degree.why: Eight of sixteen researched companies publish no named leadership, and four of the ten attacked-and-named companies have no website at all. A first-degree connection routes around both problems.
warm_first_degree.rule: Where a target is a first-degree connection, it is a LinkedIn message from the founder, not a cold email.

cold_email.rule: Only where a corporate address is published and no warm path exists.

mutual_intro.rule: Where a mutual connection exists, ask for the introduction before messaging directly.
